title: Canonical package model, selection, and graph
description:
One package model, one selection grammar, and one resolved package graph carry
every later lifecycle capability.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The child work lands one canonical package model, one repeatable ordered selection grammar, and one resolved package graph, with no second reader or resolver surviving.

planning.outcome: One package model, one selection grammar, and one resolved graph back the lifecycle.

title: Ownership, records, and safe change
description:
Ownership claims, variable resolution, and three-way decisions together make a
change to an already-applied profile safe instead of impossible.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The child work lands per-target ownership claims, one aggregate publication, resolved variables, and three-way reconfiguration and upgrade, so an applied profile can change without stranding the repository.

planning.outcome: Ownership claims and three-way decisions make a change to an applied profile safe.

title: Package authoring and offline exchange
description:
A configured repository becomes a package, and a package reaches another
repository as one verifiable file.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The child work lands capture from declared repository targets and an offline pack/add pair, so a package can be authored, refreshed, and handed to another repository without network access.

planning.outcome: A repository becomes a package and a package travels to another repository.

title: Surface, documentation, and evidence
description:
The completed lifecycle reaches adopters through one command surface, one
canonical reference, and evidence that the surface behaves as documented.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The child work lands the profile command surface, its audit event, the canonical adopter reference, behavioural acceptance coverage, and mechanical proof that no superseded lifecycle path survives.

planning.outcome: The lifecycle reaches adopters through one surface with documentation and evidence.

title: Normalize both package manifest versions into one canonical model
description:
Give the profile engine one strict decoder that turns either package manifest
version into the single canonical package model the rest of the lifecycle reads.

## Background

The manifest type is read directly as the runtime model today, so a new manifest
field is also a new runtime field and the shipped package tree constrains every
later addition. The lifecycle needs manifest fields the shipped wire does not
carry, and the shipped package must keep decoding byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A version-dispatching decoder accepts the shipped manifest wire and a second wire that adds dependency requirements, incompatibilities, a compatible-jit range, and variable declarations, and returns one canonical package model for both.
- [hard] REQ-02: An unknown field, an unknown manifest version, or a field absent from the wire it appears in is rejected with a message naming the offending field.
- [hard] REQ-03: The shipped package tree decodes without edits, and its package identity hash is unchanged from the value the current implementation produces for the same bytes.
- [hard] REQ-04: The manifest type is no longer the runtime model; every reader consumes the canonical model, and no second decoder or parallel package representation remains.

planning.outcome: One strict decoder turns either package manifest wire into the single canonical package model.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One decoder module with a frozen hash contract and colocated unit coverage.

title: Select profiles through repeatable ordered selectors
description:
Replace the single-profile argument with a repeatable ordered selector that names
either a recorded profile id or a package directory in the worktree.

## Background

Selection is one id plus an optional separate location flag, so a caller cannot
name several profiles, cannot interleave id and directory selections, and cannot
express the order it wants them considered in.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Selecting commands accept a repeatable selector naming either a profile id or a worktree-relative package directory, and the request preserves occurrence order exactly, including interleaved forms.
- [hard] REQ-02: A directory selection that shadows the id of an embedded package is rejected by name rather than silently preferred.
- [hard] REQ-03: The previous single-id argument and its separate location flag are gone from the command line, the generated schema, and the bridge tool inventory, with no alias retained.
- [hard] REQ-04: Selection reads only the worktree; a package outside it, or under the data root, is refused with the existing confinement error.

planning.outcome: Selecting commands take repeatable ordered selectors naming a profile id or a package directory.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One argument grammar threaded through existing request types with contract tests.

title: Resolve the selected package set against its declared graph
description:
Resolve a selection together with the profiles already applied, so declared
dependencies, incompatibilities, and version ranges are settled before anything
is written.

## Background

Dependency closures resolve today, but nothing expresses that two packages must
not coexist, nothing constrains which engine versions a package supports, and the
resolution does not consider profiles that are already applied but unselected.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Resolution evaluates the selected packages together with every already-applied profile, so an unselected applied profile participates in dependency, incompatibility, and range decisions.
- [hard] REQ-02: A missing dependency, a dependency cycle, a declared incompatibility between two participating packages, and a compatible-jit range the running engine falls outside of each fail before publication with a message naming the packages involved.
- [hard] REQ-03: An unsafe relative path, a symlinked package source, and an executable asset the manifest did not declare executable each fail at read time.
- [hard] REQ-04: Resolution is deterministic: the same selection and applied set produce the same resolved graph regardless of selector order.

planning.outcome: A selection resolves with its dependencies, incompatibilities, and compatible-jit ranges before publication.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure resolver over an existing closure walk with property coverage.

title: Resolve declared non-secret variables into package content
description:
Let a package declare named non-secret variables, resolve them by a fixed
precedence, and substitute them into the content the package contributes.

## Background

A package is fully literal, so one workflow that differs only in a project name or
a path needs a forked package. Making that parametric requires a declaration, an
input channel, and one bounded substitution syntax that cannot become a general
template language or a secret channel.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A package declares variables with a name, an optional default, and an optional environment-variable name, and an undeclared or duplicated declaration is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-02: A value resolves from the declared default, then a supplied values file, then the declared environment variable, then a repeated command-line assignment, with each later source overriding the earlier.
- [hard] REQ-03: One reference syntax substitutes resolved values into string values and into asset and region bodies that opt in; an identifier, a path, a mode, and a body that did not opt in reject a reference.
- [hard] REQ-04: Resolution is deterministic, so the same declarations and the same supplied inputs yield identical content, and the resolved values are returned for a caller to persist.
- [hard] REQ-05: No input is treated as sensitive: there is no secret flag, no redaction path, and no resolved value reaches the audit trail.
- [hard] REQ-06: Package identity covers the unresolved package bytes only, so supplying different values does not change which package was applied.

planning.outcome: Declared variables resolve by fixed precedence and substitute through one bounded reference syntax.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One resolver plus one substitution pass with precedence table coverage.

title: Compose contributions by semantic identity with shared ownership
description:
Decide contribution conflicts by comparing resolved definitions and recording who
owns each one, so two packages contributing the same definition coexist and a
package no longer collides with itself.

## Background

Merging compares a candidate contribution against the live registry value and
fails whenever they differ, and occupancy is resolved per file from the applied
records without excluding the candidate package. A package that changed one
contribution therefore reports a conflict against its own prior record.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Two packages contributing a structurally equal resolved definition compose successfully and the result records both as owners in a stable order.
- [hard] REQ-02: Two packages contributing different definitions for one identity conflict, and selector order does not decide a winner.
- [hard] REQ-03: Ownership is resolved per contribution identity rather than per file, and a package re-contributing an identity it already owns is not reported as conflicting with itself.
- [hard] REQ-04: A conflict names the contributing packages and the semantic identity, and distinguishes a package-owned identity from one the repository owns with no package behind it.

planning.outcome: Equal contribution definitions share sorted owners while differing definitions conflict without an order winner.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One merge function replaced in place with table-driven conflict coverage.

title: Carry ownership claims in the applied profile record
description:
Extend the applied profile record from package-level hashes to per-target and
per-identity ownership claims with the base each claim was published from.

## Background

The record states a package hash and a flat map of target hashes. Nothing records
which contribution identity a package owns, what the content looked like when the
package published it, or that a target is repository-owned and must survive. A
three-way decision has no base to compare against without that.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The record states origin, profile version, compatible-jit range, package identity, resolved non-secret inputs, and sorted per-target and per-identity ownership claims, each carrying the base fingerprint it was published from.
- [hard] REQ-02: A claim can mark content as retained when no package owns it, so repository content that no package contributed survives a later application.
- [hard] REQ-03: A record in the shipped format is read once, converted into the current format, and written back in the same transaction as the operation that encountered it; ordinary reads accept only the current format.
- [hard] REQ-04: Records remain provenance: no configured behavior is served from a record, and effective configuration continues to load from the declared registries.

planning.outcome: The applied record states per-target ownership claims with base fingerprints and reads the shipped format as input.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One record type plus a private conversion path with round-trip coverage.

title: Publish one selection through one recoverable transaction
description:
Plan a whole selection once and publish it through a single recoverable
transaction, replacing the per-package application calls.

## Background

Application already derives a shared plan and submits it through the shared
mutation session, but a selection naming several packages runs that path once per
package. A failure part-way therefore leaves some packages applied and others not.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A selection naming several packages produces one plan over the whole applied closure and publishes it through one recoverable transaction.
- [hard] REQ-02: A failure at any point leaves either the complete prior repository state or the complete new state, including repository bytes, records, and audit state.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repeating an operation whose result is already present changes nothing and reports the selection as unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: The per-package application entry point is gone, and no caller reaches publication except through the aggregate path.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every operation works in a repository with no Git directory.

planning.outcome: A whole selection reaches the repository through one recoverable transaction over the applied closure.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One orchestration path collapsed onto the existing session with failure injection.

title: Decide each target from base, current, and candidate
description:
Compare the base a claim was published from, the current repository value, and the
resolved candidate, so an applied profile can be changed, reconfigured, or
upgraded instead of being frozen at its first application.

## Background

An applied profile is effectively write-once: a record whose content differs is
rejected outright, so a package edited after application cannot be applied again,
and the repository is left reporting drift with no sanctioned way back. This is
the defect the container exists to remove.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A target whose current value still matches its recorded base updates to the candidate value.
- [hard] REQ-02: A target whose current value diverges from both its base and the candidate reports an actionable conflict naming the target, the owning package, and the three values, and publishes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-03: Content owned by several profiles retains its surviving owners when one of them stops contributing it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Content that is unchanged, solely owned, and not marked retained may be removed as part of replacing an installed version; content that is changed, shared, or retained is never removed.
- [hard] REQ-05: Re-applying a package whose content changed succeeds and rewrites its record, and repository content no package owns survives that operation.

planning.outcome: Reconfiguration and upgrade decide each target from its recorded base, current value, and resolved candidate.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure decision function with an exhaustive base-current-candidate table.

title: Capture a package tree from declared repository targets
description:
Turn the repository-local package assembler into a supported operation that
publishes a package tree from the repository files its manifest declares.

## Background

The assembler already reads declared live targets, stages a tree, validates it as
a package, and publishes it whole, and a changed live file changes the resulting
package identity. It is compiled only for this crate's tests, is hardcoded to this
repository's own package path, follows symlinks, and does not screen executable
content. Without it, a package is hand-authored and an in-place edit to
profile-owned content cannot be folded back into the package that owns it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Capture reads the repository targets a manifest declares and publishes a package tree containing exactly the manifest, the declared asset sources, and the declared region sources; a source the manifest stopped declaring does not survive.
- [hard] REQ-02: Capture serves any repository and any package id from supplied arguments; no repository path, package id, or entry-point script is compiled in, and the operation is present in an ordinary binary rather than behind a test feature.
- [hard] REQ-03: A declared target that is a symlink, resolves outside the worktree, or carries executable permission the manifest did not declare is refused before anything is staged.
- [hard] REQ-04: The published tree decodes and validates as a package, and capture publishes through the shared recoverable transaction rather than its own publication path, so a failure cannot lose an occupied destination.
- [hard] REQ-05: Capturing a package whose owned content was edited in place produces a tree whose identity reflects that edit, so re-applying it reconciles the repository.

planning.outcome: Capture publishes a package tree from the repository targets a manifest declares.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One existing assembler generalized and exposed with integration coverage.

title: Pack a package into a verifiable archive
description:
Give a package one portable file that carries its identity and digest, and one
operation that verifies that file before placing the package in the worktree.

## Background

Sharing a package means copying a directory, with nothing that states what was
copied or confirms it arrived intact. Package identity is already a content digest
over the manifest and every file, and an archive dependency is already present, so
the exchange format can reuse both rather than introduce a second digest or a new
container library.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Packing a package directory produces one archive file carrying the package id, its version, and the package identity digest, and packing the same package twice produces byte-identical output.
- [hard] REQ-02: Adding an archive recomputes the package identity from the extracted content and refuses the archive when it disagrees with the digest the archive carries.
- [hard] REQ-03: An archive entry with an absolute path, a parent-directory traversal, a symlink, or an unexpected mode is refused, and nothing is written outside the named destination.
- [hard] REQ-04: A refused or interrupted add leaves no partially extracted package, and an occupied destination is never overwritten.
- [hard] REQ-05: Packing and adding read and write local files only: no network access, no registry lookup, and no search of undeclared filesystem locations.

planning.outcome: A package packs into one digest-carrying archive that add verifies before placing it in the worktree.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One archive reader and writer over the existing dependency with adversarial fixtures.

title: Check applied profiles against their packages and the repository
description:
Report whether the profiles this repository records still agree with the packages
they came from and with the repository content they own.

## Background

Repository-wide validation reports profile provenance and derived-state drift
among everything else it checks. Once profiles carry per-identity ownership and a
base fingerprint, a profile-scoped check can say which profile diverged and how,
which is what an adopter needs before choosing to reconfigure or upgrade.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The check reports, per recorded profile, whether its package is readable at the location the record names, whether the package still matches the recorded identity, and whether each owned target still matches its recorded base.
- [hard] REQ-02: An ownership claim naming a target that no longer exists, and a target claimed by a record whose package is gone, are each reported rather than ignored.
- [hard] REQ-03: The check writes nothing and reports a non-zero status when any profile diverges, so it is usable as a repository check.
- [hard] REQ-04: Repository-wide validation keeps reporting the same divergences through the shared logic, with no second implementation of the comparison.

planning.outcome: A profile-scoped check reports which recorded profile diverged from its package or its owned content.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One comparison over claims the record already carries.

title: Report what an operation would change before it runs
description:
Add the read-only report that answers what a selection would do to this
repository, so an adopter can inspect a decision before publishing it.

## Background

The command family cannot answer what an operation would change. Once
reconfiguration and upgrade exist, every mutation has a decision behind it that a
reader needs to see before it is published.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A difference report states, for each participating profile, the targets and identities that would update, conflict, be retained, or be removed, and writes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-02: The report distinguishes a target no package owns from one a package owns, and names the owning packages for shared content.
- [hard] REQ-03: The report is produced from the same decision the mutating path would publish, so a reported decision and the published outcome cannot disagree.
- [hard] REQ-04: The report is available for a selection that is not yet applied, so an adopter can inspect a package before applying it.

planning.outcome: A read-only report states what a selection would change before anything is published.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One read-only projection over decisions the prior work already computes.

title: Give the profile subcommands one presentation contract
description:
Unify how every profile subcommand presents itself: human output, machine
envelopes, rehearsal mode, generated schema, and the bridge tool inventory.

## Background

The family grows from three subcommands to the full lifecycle, and each new one
arrives with its own wiring. Left alone they drift into different envelopes,
different rehearsal semantics, and hand-maintained bridge entries. This work runs
after the subcommands exist so it can standardize what is actually there.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every profile subcommand emits machine-readable output under the project's collection envelope, and list-emitting subcommands share one envelope shape.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each mutating subcommand supports a rehearsal mode that reports the decisions it would publish and writes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-03: Human output states profile id, version, origin, and per-target decision consistently, and no subcommand uses a decision vocabulary the others do not.
- [hard] REQ-04: The generated command schema and the bridge tool inventory expose the family from the command definitions, with no hand-written duplicate of a subcommand's arguments.

planning.outcome: The profile subcommands present themselves through one envelope, rehearsal, and schema contract.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One presentation pass over subcommands that already exist.

title: Record one lifecycle event per changed mutation
description:
Replace the per-application audit record with one event describing what a
lifecycle operation actually changed.

## Background

Mutations append an application event per package, which cannot describe a
selection that reconfigured one profile, upgraded another, and left a third alone.
The event also has to carry variable provenance without carrying values.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A mutation that changes the aggregate appends exactly one event naming the requested operation and, per profile in a stable order, whether it was installed, unchanged, reconfigured, or upgraded.
- [hard] REQ-02: A rehearsal, and a mutation that leaves the aggregate entirely unchanged, append no event.
- [hard] REQ-03: The event names variables by name and by which source supplied them, and carries no resolved value and no rendered content.
- [hard] REQ-04: Conversion of a record in the shipped format is reported inside the event for the operation that encountered it rather than as an operation of its own.
- [hard] REQ-05: The prior per-application event is no longer constructed or appended; the existing log continues to decode historical entries.

planning.outcome: A changed mutation appends one lifecycle event naming the operation, per-profile action, and variable sources.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One event variant replacing another with catalog and parser coverage.

title: Document the completed profile lifecycle for adopters
description:
Make the canonical profile reference describe the lifecycle that now ships, and
keep neighbouring pages citing it rather than restating it.

## Background

The canonical reference currently states an apply-only boundary and lists the
capabilities this container delivers as explicitly absent. Several other pages
describe obtaining and applying a package, so the facts have to move as one set.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The canonical profile reference describes authoring, capture, exchange, composition, variables, ownership, drift, reconfiguration, and upgrade as current behavior, and the section declaring those capabilities absent is gone.
- [hard] REQ-02: Pages that mention profiles link to the canonical reference instead of restating lifecycle facts, and volatile inventories are generated or cited rather than hand-copied.
- [hard] REQ-03: Documentation states current behavior only, with no narration of what the surface used to do.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every path and command named in the changed pages resolves, and the repository's citation check reports no missing target.

planning.outcome: The canonical profile reference states the lifecycle that now ships and neighbouring pages cite it.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One canonical page rewritten with linked pages swept in the same pass.

title: Prove publication survives interruption
description:
Inject failures into lifecycle publication and show the repository lands on one
complete state.

## Background

The lifecycle publishes through one recoverable transaction and claims
all-or-nothing behavior with idempotent retry. Only injected failure demonstrates
that claim. The suite is a module of the existing workflow target, so the enforced
integration-target budget is unaffected.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A failure injected at each publication stage leaves either the complete prior repository state or the complete new state across repository bytes, ownership records, and audit state.
- [hard] REQ-02: Retrying an interrupted operation reaches the same result as an uninterrupted run.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repeating a completed operation reports it as unchanged and writes nothing further.
- [hard] REQ-04: The suite is a module of an existing integration-test target.

planning.outcome: Injected publication failures leave the repository on one complete state and retry converges.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Injection cases over one already-delivered transaction boundary.

title: Prove concurrent lifecycle callers serialize
description:
Show that two lifecycle operations issued against one repository at the same time
serialize rather than interleave.

## Background

Repository mutation is guarded, and the lifecycle adds operations that plan against
a captured image before publishing. A second caller arriving between capture and
publication is the case that has to be demonstrated rather than assumed. The suite
is a module of the existing workflow target.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Two lifecycle operations issued concurrently against one repository complete in some serial order, and neither observes a state the other left partially written.
- [hard] REQ-02: A caller that loses the race either waits and proceeds against the updated state or fails with a message naming the contention, and never publishes a plan built on a stale capture.
- [hard] REQ-03: The suite is a module of an existing integration-test target.

planning.outcome: Concurrent lifecycle callers complete in a serial order without observing partial state.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Contention cases over one already-guarded mutation path.

title: Prove the lifecycle runs without version control
description:
Show every lifecycle operation working in a repository that has no version-control
directory.

## Background

Core commands must work without Git, with claims and leases the documented
exception. The lifecycle adds operations that read package directories and publish
repository content, none of which needs version control, so the guarantee has to be
extended to them by evidence. The suite is a module of the existing workflow target.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Selection, resolution, application, reconfiguration, upgrade, capture, packing, adding, difference reporting, and the profile check each complete in a repository with no version-control directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: No lifecycle operation reports a version-control error or silently degrades when version control is absent.
- [hard] REQ-03: The suite is a module of an existing integration-test target.

planning.outcome: Each lifecycle operation completes in a repository with no version-control directory.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Environment cases over operations the prior work delivered.

title: Prove no superseded lifecycle path survives
description:
Add mechanical checks that fail if a second package reader, a compatibility shim,
or a superseded lifecycle path reappears.

## Background

The container forbids adapters, dual formats, fallback behavior, and duplicated
inventories, and this repository already enforces one such absence with a
structural contract test. That mechanism is the way the constraint stays true
after the work lands.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A structural check fails if a second package decoder, package model, or applied-record reader is present alongside the canonical one.
- [hard] REQ-02: A structural check fails if the superseded single-profile selection argument, the per-package application entry point, or the prior application event constructor reappears.
- [hard] REQ-03: A structural check fails if any input is described as secret or sensitive across the manifest, the command line, the generated schema, the bridge inventory, or the audit trail.
- [hard] REQ-04: The checks name what they forbid and why, so a failure tells a reader which constraint was breached rather than only which symbol matched.

planning.outcome: Mechanical checks reject a duplicate resolver, a compatibility shim, or a surviving predecessor path.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Assertions appended to the existing structural suite with named rationale.
